q: What is the first step in solving a computational problem?
s: You cannot design a correct solution until you know exactly what is given and what is required.

q: An algorithm is:
o: A finite sequence of steps to solve a problem
s: An algorithm is a finite, well-defined sequence of steps that solves a problem.

q: Which property requires an algorithm to terminate after a finite number of steps?
s: Finiteness: the algorithm must end after a limited number of steps.

q: An algorithm should produce:
s: Every algorithm must give at least one output, otherwise it solves nothing.

q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a good algorithm?
s: Steps must be unambiguous (definite). Ambiguity is a defect, not a characteristic.

q: Pseudocode is:
o: An informal, language-independent way to describe an algorithm
s: Pseudocode describes logic in plain structured English, not tied to any language.

q: Which symbol is commonly used for input/output in a flowchart?
s: The parallelogram represents input and output.

q: Which flowchart symbol represents a process?
s: The rectangle is the processing (calculation or assignment) box.

q: A diamond in a flowchart represents:
s: The diamond holds a condition with Yes/No (True/False) exits.

q: Which symbol usually represents the start or end of a flowchart?
s: The oval (terminator) marks Start and End.

q: Flow lines in a flowchart indicate:
s: Arrows show the order in which steps are executed.

q: Which tool is most suitable for representing the logical steps of a solution visually?
s: A flowchart is the graphical representation of an algorithm.

q: Pseudocode is primarily intended to:
o: Be executed directly by a CPU
s: Its purpose is to communicate logic to humans before coding.

q: In an algorithm, a decision is generally based on:
s: Decisions test a condition that is true or false.

q: Which control structure executes instructions one after another?
s: Sequence means statements run in the order written.

q: Repeating a set of instructions is known as:
s: Iteration (looping) repeats steps.

q: Choosing between alternative paths based on a condition is:
s: Selection (branching) such as if-else.

q: What is the main purpose of dry-running an algorithm?
o: To translate it into machine code
To trace its steps manually and verify logic
s: A dry run traces values by hand to catch logic errors before coding.

q: Which of these is a valid example of an algorithm step?
o: Add A and B, then display the sum
s: A valid step is clear, precise and executable.

q: A flowchart is useful because it:
s: It presents the logic visually so it is easy to follow and check.

q: The C programming language was developed by:
s: Dennis Ritchie created C. Stroustrup made C++, Gosling Java, van Rossum Python.

q: C was developed at:
s: C was developed at AT&T Bell Laboratories.

q: C was developed primarily in which decade?
s: Ritchie developed C in the early 1970s (around 1972).

q: C is commonly described as a:
s: C combines high-level constructs with low-level memory access, so it is called middle-level.

q: Which of the following is a common extension for a C source file?
s: C source files use .c (.cpp is C++).

q: Which function is the usual entry point of a hosted C program?
s: Execution begins at main().

q: Which header is needed for standard printf() and scanf() declarations?
s: stdio.h declares the standard input/output functions.

q: Which punctuation mark commonly terminates a C statement?
s: A semicolon ends a statement.

q: C is:
s: Main and main are different names in C.

q: Which of the following is a valid basic structure element of a C program?
s: A C program has preprocessor directives, global declarations, main() and functions.

q: A comment in C that begins with // continues until:
s: A // comment ends at the end of the line.

q: Which notation is used for a multi-line comment in C?
s: /* ... */ can span several lines.

q: The preprocessor handles directives that generally begin with:
s: Directives such as #include and #define start with #.

q: Which directive is commonly used to include a header file?
s: #include copies a header file into the source.

q: What is the main role of a compiler?
o: To execute source code without translation
To translate source code into a lower-level form
s: A compiler translates source code into assembly or machine-level code.

q: Which stage commonly converts preprocessed C code into assembly code?
s: The compilation stage produces assembly from preprocessed code.

q: The assembler converts:
s: Assembly becomes machine-level object code (.o or .obj).

q: The linker mainly:
o: Combines object files and resolves external references
s: The linker joins object files and libraries into one executable.

q: The loader is responsible for:
o: Loading an executable into memory for execution
s: The loader places the executable in memory and starts it.

q: Which sequence best represents a traditional C build process?
s: Preprocess, compile, assemble, link (then load and run).

q: A syntax error is generally detected during:
s: The compiler reports syntax errors.

q: A linker error may occur when:
o: An external function definition cannot be found
A variable has a valid value
s: A typical linker error is 'undefined reference' to a function.

q: Which file commonly contains compiled object code?
s: Object files use .o (GCC) or .obj (MSVC).

q: What does IDE stand for?
s: An IDE bundles editor, compiler and debugger.

q: Which of the following is a C compiler?
s: GCC is the GNU C compiler.

q: The smallest individual units of a C program are called:
s: Tokens: keywords, identifiers, constants, strings, operators, punctuators.

q: Which of the following is a C token?
s: A keyword is one kind of token.

q: Which of these is a C keyword?
s: int is reserved. main is a function name, not a keyword.

q: Which of the following is NOT a C keyword?
s: student is an ordinary identifier.

q: Keywords in C are:
s: Keywords have fixed meanings and cannot be used as names.

q: Which is a valid C identifier?
s: Identifiers use letters, digits and underscores, cannot start with a digit and cannot be keywords.

q: Which character may appear in a C identifier?
s: Only letters, digits and underscore are allowed.

q: A C identifier cannot:
o: Contain digits after the first character
s: An identifier must not start with a digit.

q: Which name is invalid as an identifier because it is a keyword?
s: return is reserved.

q: C identifiers are:
s: Total and total are different identifiers.

q: A constant is a value that:
o: Does not change during its intended use
s: A constant stays fixed.

q: Which is an integer constant?
s: 25 has no decimal point. 3.14 is floating, 'A' is a character, "Hello" is a string.

q: Which is a character constant in C?
s: Character constants use single quotes.

q: Which is a string literal?
s: String literals use double quotes.

q: Which suffix can indicate an unsigned integer constant?
s: 25U is unsigned. F is for float constants.

q: A variable is:
o: A named memory location whose value can change
s: A variable names a storage location whose value may change.

q: Which is a valid variable declaration?
s: Syntax: type name;

q: In the declaration int x = 10;, the value 10 is:
s: 10 is an integer constant. x is the identifier.

q: Which statement assigns 20 to variable x?
s: Assignment puts the value on the right into the variable on the left.

q: Which of the following is a valid identifier for a variable?
s: _count starts with an underscore and has no spaces or keywords.

q: Which category contains int, char, and float?
s: These are the basic (primary) data types.

q: Which C type is commonly used to store a single character?
s: char holds one character.

q: Which type is generally used for single-precision floating-point values?
s: float is single precision.

q: Which type generally provides more precision than float?
s: double has about twice the precision of float.

q: The void type indicates:
s: void means no value (for example a function returning nothing).

q: Which of the following is a derived data type in C?
s: Arrays, pointers and functions are derived types.

q: Which operator is used to declare a pointer variable?
s: int *p; declares a pointer to int.

q: A function type is associated with:
s: Functions have a type made of return type and parameter types.

q: Which keyword is used to define a structure?
s: struct groups variables of different types.

q: Which keyword is used to define a union?
s: union members share the same memory.

q: Which keyword is used to define an enumeration?
s: enum defines named integer constants.

q: Which of the following is a user-defined type mechanism in C?
s: struct, union and enum create user-defined types.

q: What does typedef do?
o: Defines an alias for a type name
s: typedef gives a new name to an existing type.

q: Which declaration creates an array of 10 integers?
s: Array syntax: type name[size];

q: Which declaration creates a pointer to int?
s: int *p; declares p as a pointer to int.

q: Which header file declares getchar() and putchar()?
s: Both are in stdio.h.

q: Which function is used for formatted output in C?
s: printf writes formatted output.

q: Which function is used for formatted input in C?
s: scanf reads formatted input.

q: Which format specifier is commonly used with printf() for an int?
s: %d prints a signed decimal integer.

q: Which format specifier is commonly used for a float value in printf()?
s: %f prints floating-point values.

q: Which format specifier is used to print a character?
s: %c prints one character.

q: Which format specifier is commonly used to print a string?
s: %s prints a null-terminated string.

q: In scanf("%d", &x);, what is the purpose of &?
o: It obtains the address of x
s: scanf needs the address of x so it can store the value there.

q: Which statement correctly reads an integer into variable n?
s: Pass the address of n with &.

q: Which function reads a single character from standard input?
s: getchar() reads one character.

q: Which function writes a single character to standard output?
s: putchar() writes one character.

q: getchar() returns:
o: A character value represented as int, or EOF
s: It returns an int so that EOF (-1) can be told apart from valid characters.

q: Which function is unformatted character output?
s: putchar writes a raw character with no format string.

q: Which of the following is a formatted I/O function?
s: printf (and scanf) use format specifiers.

q: What does EOF commonly indicate?
o: End of file or input condition
s: EOF signals that no more input is available (or an error).

q: Which escape sequence moves the cursor to a new line in printf()?
s: \n is the newline.

q: Which escape sequence represents a horizontal tab?
s: \t is the horizontal tab.

q: What is the output of printf("%d", 5 + 3);?
s: The expression 5 + 3 is evaluated first and %d prints 8.

q: Which statement about scanf() is correct?
o: It is used only for output
It commonly uses format specifiers to read input
s: scanf uses format specifiers such as %d, %f and %c.

q: Which pair correctly matches the function with its purpose?
s: getchar reads one character. printf outputs, scanf inputs, putchar writes.

q: Which operator is used for addition in C?
s: + adds two operands.

q: What is the result of 10 % 3 in C?
s: 10 = 3 x 3 + 1, so the remainder is 1.

q: Which operator is used for multiplication?
s: * multiplies. C has no ** operator.

q: Which operator gives the remainder after integer division?
s: % is the modulus (remainder) operator.

q: What is the result of 7 / 2 when both operands are integers?
s: Integer division discards the fraction: 3.

q: Which operator has higher precedence?
s: Multiplicative operators bind tighter than additive, assignment and logical OR.

q: Which of the following is a relational operator?
s: == is relational. && is logical, += is assignment, % is arithmetic.

q: What does the expression 5 > 3 evaluate to in C?
s: A true relational expression gives 1.

q: Which operator checks equality between two values?
s: == compares. = assigns.

q: Which operator means "not equal to"?
s: != is not-equal in C.

q: Which operator represents logical AND?
s: && is logical AND. & is bitwise AND.

q: Which operator represents logical OR?
s: || is logical OR. | is bitwise OR.

q: Which operator performs logical NOT?
s: ! is logical NOT. ~ is bitwise complement.

q: In C, a non-zero value used as a condition is treated as:
s: Zero is false, any non-zero value is true.

q: What is the result of !0 in C?
s: !0 is 1 (true).

q: Which operator assigns a value to a variable?
s: = is the assignment operator.

q: What does x += 5 mean?
s: x += 5 is shorthand for x = x + 5.

q: Which is a compound assignment operator?
s: += combines an operation with assignment. C has no ===, => or &&=.

q: What is the value of x after int x = 4; x *= 3;?
Which operator is the conditional or ternary operator?
s: The ternary operator is ?:.

q: How many operands does the ternary operator use?
s: condition ? value1 : value2 has three operands.

q: Which expression correctly uses the ternary operator?
s: Syntax: condition ? expr1 : expr2.

q: What is the result of (4 > 2) ? 10 : 20?
s: 4 > 2 is true, so the first value 10 is chosen.

q: Which operator performs bitwise AND?
s: & ANDs each pair of bits.

q: Which operator performs bitwise OR?
s: | ORs each pair of bits.

q: Which operator performs bitwise XOR?
s: ^ is bitwise exclusive OR.

q: Which operator performs bitwise complement?
s: ~ flips every bit.

q: Which operator shifts bits to the left?
s: << is left shift.

q: Which operator shifts bits to the right?
s: >> is right shift.

q: What is the binary representation of decimal 5?
s: 5 = 4 + 1 = 101 in binary.

q: What is the result of 5 & 3?
What is the result of 5 | 3?
What is the result of 5 ^ 3?
Which operator has higher precedence in C?
s: * is higher than +, = and the comma operator (lowest).

q: Which statement about the expression a + b * c is correct?
s: * has higher precedence, so it is b * c first.

q: Which statement is used for basic decision-making?
s: if tests a condition and chooses what to execute.

q: The if statement executes its block when the condition is:
s: Any non-zero value counts as true.

q: Which keyword provides an alternative block when an if condition is false?
s: else runs when the if condition is false.

q: Which is the correct basic syntax of an if statement?
s: The condition goes in parentheses, followed by a block.

q: An if-else statement is used to:
s: It chooses between two paths.

q: An if statement inside another if statement is called:
s: This is a nested if.

q: Which keyword begins a multi-way selection statement in C?
s: switch selects among several case labels.

q: Which keyword labels an individual option in a switch statement?
s: Each option is written as case value:.

q: Which keyword specifies the fallback branch in a switch statement?
s: default runs when no case matches.

q: Which statement commonly terminates a switch case to prevent fall-through?
s: break leaves the switch.

q: Which data types are permitted as the controlling expression of a standard C switch statement?
s: switch needs an integer expression (char and enum are integer types).

q: What happens if break is omitted at the end of a matching switch case?
o: Execution may continue into subsequent case labels
s: Control falls through to the next case.

q: Can two case labels in the same switch have the same constant value?
s: Duplicate case values are a compile-time error.

q: How many default labels may appear in one switch statement?
s: default is optional and can appear at most once.

q: Which statement is generally suitable for checking a range of conditions?
s: Ranges such as marks >= 90 need relational tests, which an if-else-if ladder handles.

q: Which loop checks its condition before executing the loop body?
o: Both do-while and while check after the body
s: while is entry-controlled.

q: Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least once?
s: do-while tests the condition after the body.

q: Which keyword begins a for loop?
s: for (init; condition; update).

q: Which is the correct general syntax of a for loop?
s: Three parts separated by semicolons inside parentheses.

q: In a for loop, which part is evaluated first?
s: Initialization runs once, then the condition is checked.

q: Which loop is often convenient when the number of iterations is known?
s: for keeps initialization, condition and update together.

q: What happens if the condition of a while loop is initially false?
s: The check comes first, so the body is skipped.

q: What is the purpose of the update expression in a typical counting loop?
s: It changes the counter so the loop can finish.

q: What is a nested loop?
o: A loop placed inside another loop
s: One loop inside another.

q: If an outer loop runs 3 times and an inner loop runs 2 times per outer iteration, how many times does the inner body execute in total?
Which loop is an entry-controlled loop?
s: while (and for) test the condition on entry.

q: Which loop is an exit-controlled loop?
s: do-while tests after the body.

q: What punctuation ends the condition in a do-while statement?
s: do { ... } while (condition); needs the final semicolon.

q: Which statement correctly describes an infinite loop?
o: A loop whose termination condition is never reached
A loop that executes exactly once
s: The loop never ends because the exit condition is never met.

q: What is the output of this code? int i = 1; while (i <= 3) { printf("%d", i); i++; }
s: It prints 1, 2 and 3 one after another with no separators: 123.

q: What is the output of this code? int i = 1; do { printf("%d", i); i++; } while (i < 1);
s: The body runs once and prints 1. Then i = 2 and 2 < 1 is false.

q: Which loop component is optional in a for statement?
o: The loop body in every form
s: Each of the three expressions may be left empty, but the semicolons stay.

q: What is the result of placing a semicolon immediately after a for loop header?
o: It always causes a syntax error
It creates an empty loop body
It converts the loop into a switch
s: The semicolon is the loop body (an empty statement), so the following block runs once.

q: Which loop is commonly used to traverse a two-dimensional array?
s: One loop for rows and one for columns.

q: If a loop variable is never updated and the condition remains true, the loop may become:
s: The condition never becomes false.

q: Which statement immediately exits the nearest enclosing loop or switch?
s: break leaves the innermost loop or switch.

q: Which statement skips the remaining statements in the current loop iteration?
s: continue jumps to the next iteration.

q: In a for loop, continue transfers control to:
o: The loop update expression, then condition check
s: In a for loop the update runs before the condition is re-tested.

q: In a while loop, continue transfers control to:
s: Control goes directly to re-evaluating the condition.

q: Which statement transfers control to a labeled statement?
s: goto label; jumps to the label.

q: Which keyword is used to define a label target for goto?
o: A valid identifier followed by a colon
s: A label is written as name: (for example end:). There is no label keyword.

q: Which statement is generally preferred over excessive use of goto?
s: if, loops and switch keep programs readable. Heavy goto use creates tangled code.

q: A break statement inside nested loops exits:
s: break affects only the innermost loop (or switch).

q: What happens when continue is executed inside a loop?
o: The current iteration is abandoned and the next iteration proceeds
s: The rest of the body is skipped for this iteration only.

q: Which statement can be used inside both loops and switch statements?
s: break works in both. continue works only in loops.

q: An expression in C is:
o: A combination of operands and operators that produces a value
s: Operands joined by operators yield a value.

q: Which of the following is an arithmetic expression?
s: It combines variables and constants with arithmetic operators.

q: What is the value of 2 + 3 * 4?
Parentheses in an expression are commonly used to:
o: Convert every value to a string
s: Parenthesised parts are evaluated first.

q: Type conversion means:
o: Changing a value from one data type to another
s: Converting a value from one type to another.

q: Implicit type conversion is performed:
o: Automatically by the compiler according to language rules
Only by using a cast operator
Only by the programmer at runtime
s: The compiler promotes types automatically (usual arithmetic conversions).

q: Explicit type conversion is also known as:
s: Explicit conversion is type casting.

q: Which expression performs an explicit conversion of x to float?
s: A cast puts the type in parentheses: (float)x.

q: In the expression 5 + 2.5, the integer operand is generally converted to:
o: float or the corresponding common floating type
s: The int is converted to the floating type of the other operand (double here).

q: What is the result of (float)5 / 2 in C?
s: The cast makes 5 a float, so the division is floating-point: 2.5.

q: What is the result of 5 / 2 when both operands are int?
s: Integer division truncates to 2.

q: Assigning a double value to an int variable may cause:
o: The int variable to become a string
s: The fractional part is truncated (and an out-of-range value is undefined).

q: Which conversion may lose information?
o: Converting int to a wider integer type
s: double to int drops the fraction. The others widen the type.

q: In C, the cast operator is written using:
s: For example (int)3.7.

q: Which statement about implicit conversion is correct?
o: It can occur in arithmetic expressions and assignments
It is performed only by printf()
s: Mixed-type arithmetic and assignments trigger automatic conversions.

q: What is the value of x after this code? int x = 5; x = x + 2.8;
s: x + 2.8 is 7.8 (double). Storing it in an int truncates to 7.

q: Which operator has right-to-left associativity among these?
s: Assignment associates right to left (a = b = c means a = (b = c)).

q: What is the result of the expression (10 > 5) && (3 < 1)?
Which operator is evaluated before logical AND in the expression a > 2 && b < 5?
s: Relational operators have higher precedence than &&.

q: Which statement about the conditional operator ?: is correct?
o: It selects one of two expressions based on a condition
s: It is the only ternary operator and picks one of two expressions.

q: An array in C is used to store:
o: Values of different data types only
Multiple values of the same data type
s: An array holds several elements of one type.

q: Array elements are stored in:
s: Elements sit next to each other in memory.

q: The index of the first element of a C array is:
s: C arrays are zero-indexed.

q: Which is a valid declaration of an integer array with 5 elements?
s: Syntax: type name[size];

q: What is the last valid index of int a[10];?
s: Indices run from 0 to size - 1, so 0 to 9.

q: How many elements are present in int marks[7];?
s: The declared size is the number of elements.

q: What is the value of a[2] after int a[4] = {10, 20, 30, 40};?
Which expression accesses the first element of array x?
s: The first element is at index 0.

q: If int a[5] = {1, 2}; is declared, the remaining elements are initialized to:
s: With a partial initializer, the rest are set to 0.

q: What is the correct way to find the number of elements in an array a in the same scope where it is an actual array?
s: Total bytes divided by bytes per element. This fails for an array parameter, which is really a pointer.

q: What is the result of accessing an array element outside its valid bounds in C?
o: It always produces a compile-time error
s: C does not check bounds. The behaviour is undefined.

q: A one-dimensional array is also called:
s: A 1-D array is a linear array.

q: Which statement assigns 50 to the third element of array x?
s: The third element has index 2.

q: Which loop is commonly used to traverse all elements of an array?
s: A for loop with the index as counter is the standard way.

q: In C, the name of an array expression usually converts to:
o: The value of its last element
A pointer to its first element
s: An array name decays to a pointer to its first element (except with sizeof and &).

q: A two-dimensional array is commonly used to represent:
o: A table of rows and columns
s: A 2-D array models a matrix or table.

q: Which is a valid declaration of a 3 × 4 integer array?
s: Each dimension gets its own brackets.

q: How many elements are in int matrix[3][4];?
In matrix[2][3], the first index generally identifies the:
s: The first index is the row, the second is the column.

q: In C, a two-dimensional array is stored in:
s: C stores row after row (row-major).

q: In row-major representation, elements of each row are stored:
s: Each row occupies consecutive locations, and rows follow one another.

q: Which expression accesses the element in the second row and third column of a C array named a?
s: Indices start at 0, so row 2 is 1 and column 3 is 2.

q: Which loop structure is commonly used to traverse a two-dimensional array?
s: Outer loop for rows, inner loop for columns.
Row 1 is {4,5,6}, and index 1 of it is 5.

q: The total memory occupied by int a[2][3], assuming sizeof(int) is 4 bytes, is:
s: 6 elements x 4 bytes = 24 bytes.

q: Which operation on an array means visiting each element one by one?
s: Traversal visits every element.

q: Searching an array means:
o: Finding whether a target value exists and/or its position
s: Searching looks for a target value and often returns its index.

q: Which operation changes the order of elements in an array?
s: Sorting rearranges the elements.

q: Inserting an element into the middle of a fixed-size array may require:
s: Later elements must move one place to make room.

q: Which statement about a C array is correct?
o: Its size can automatically grow whenever an element is added
Its elements are accessed using indices
It can store only one element
s: Elements are accessed by index. Size is fixed and indexing starts at 0.

q: A C string is:
o: A character sequence terminated by the null character
A character sequence terminated by a space
s: A C string is a char array ending with '\0'.

q: Which character marks the end of a C string?
s: The null character '\0' terminates a string.

q: Which header file declares standard string-handling functions?
s: strlen, strcpy, strcat and strcmp are in string.h.

q: Which declaration can store the string "Hello" including its terminator?
s: Five letters plus the null character need 6 bytes.

q: How many characters are in the string literal "Cat", excluding the null terminator?
s: C, a and t make 3.

q: How many bytes are required to store "Cat" as a C string, assuming one byte per char?
s: 3 characters + 1 null terminator = 4.

q: Which function returns the length of a string, excluding the terminating null character?
s: strlen counts characters before '\0'.

q: What does strlen("Hello") return?
s: Hello has 5 characters.

q: Which function copies one string into another?
s: strcpy(dest, src) copies src into dest.

q: Which function concatenates two strings?
s: strcat appends one string to another.

q: Which function compares two strings lexicographically?
s: strcmp compares strings character by character.

q: What does strcmp() return when two strings are equal?
s: It returns 0 for equal strings.

q: Which statement correctly copies source into destination?
s: The destination is the first argument.

q: Before using strcat(destination, source), destination must have:
o: Enough space for the combined string and null terminator
s: strcat does not check size, so a too-small buffer overflows.

q: Which function is used to find the number of characters in a string?
s: strlen gives the length.

q: What is the output of strlen("")?
s: An empty string has no characters before the terminator.

q: Which of the following is a valid string declaration?
s: C has no built-in string type, so a char array is used. The size is inferred as 5.

q: What is the purpose of the null character in a C string?
o: It indicates the end of the string
It indicates the beginning of an array
s: String functions stop when they reach '\0'.

q: Which statement about gets() is correct?
o: It is the recommended safe input function
It was removed from the C standard because it cannot limit input length
s: gets cannot limit input and causes buffer overflows. It was removed in C11.

q: Which function is generally preferred for bounded string input from standard input?
s: fgets takes a size limit and so avoids overflow.

q: A function in C is:
o: A named block of code that performs a task
s: A function is a named, reusable block of code.

q: Modular programming means:
o: Writing the entire program in one large function
Dividing a program into smaller manageable modules
s: The program is split into smaller modules (functions).

q: Which is a benefit of using functions?
s: Write once, call many times.

q: A function prototype tells the compiler about:
o: Function name, return type, and parameter types
The number of files on disk
The values of all local variables
s: It declares the name, return type and parameter types.

q: Which is a valid function prototype for a function that adds two integers and returns an int?
s: Syntax: return_type name(parameter types);

q: Which part of a function includes its executable statements?
s: The definition contains the body.

q: A function call is used to:
s: A call runs the function.

q: Which keyword is used to send a value back from a function?
s: return sends a value to the caller and ends the function.

q: Which return type indicates that a function does not return a value?
s: void means no return value.

q: Which is a valid function definition?
o: int square(int x) { return x * x; }
s: It has a return type, name, parameters and a body.

q: In a function declaration, the values listed in parentheses are called:
s: They are parameters (formal parameters).

q: The actual values supplied when a function is called are called:
s: They are arguments (actual parameters).

q: Which statement about a function prototype is correct?
o: It must contain the function body
It can allow a function to be called before its definition
It stores the function's return value
s: With a prototype, a function can be called before its definition appears.

q: Which function is the usual starting point of a hosted C program?
s: Execution begins in main().

q: A local variable declared inside a function is generally accessible:
s: Its scope is the block in which it is declared.

q: A function that calls itself is called:
s: This is recursion.

q: What is essential for a recursive function to stop calling itself?
s: A base case ends the recursion.

q: What may happen if a recursive function has no reachable base case?
o: It may continue until stack exhaustion
It is ignored by the compiler
s: Calls pile up on the call stack until it overflows.

q: The factorial of 0 is:
s: By definition 0! = 1.

q: What is 5! (5 factorial)?
Which is the recursive definition of factorial for n > 0?
What is the base case commonly used in a factorial function?
s: factorial(0) = 1 (factorial(1) = 1 also works).

q: What is the value of factorial(4)?
The Fibonacci sequence commonly begins with:
s: The usual form is 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, ...

q: In the standard Fibonacci sequence, each term after the first two is:
o: The product of the previous two terms
The sum of the previous two terms
The difference of the previous two terms

q: What is the fifth term of the sequence 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, … when counting 0 as the first term?
s: 1st 0, 2nd 1, 3rd 1, 4th 2, 5th 3.

q: Which is a common recursive definition of Fibonacci numbers?
s: Each term is the sum of the previous two.

q: Which is a valid base-case pair for the standard Fibonacci definition?
s: The standard base cases are F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1.

q: Each recursive function call generally creates:
o: A new activation record on the call stack
s: Every call gets its own stack frame with its own parameters and locals.

q: Which statement about recursion is correct?
o: It always uses less memory than iteration
It involves a function calling itself directly or indirectly
It does not need a stopping condition
s: Recursion means a function calls itself, directly or through another function.

q: In C, arguments are passed to ordinary functions by:
s: C always passes by value. Pointers are used to simulate by-reference.

q: In call by value, a function receives:
o: A copy of the argument's value
A complete copy of the program
s: The function works on a copy.

q: If a function changes its value parameter, the caller's original variable is generally:
s: Only the copy changes.

q: C can achieve reference-like modification of a caller's variable by passing:
s: Pass the address with & and modify it through the pointer.

q: Which operator obtains the address of a variable?
s: &x is the address of x.

q: Which operator is used to dereference a pointer?
s: *p accesses the value that p points to.

q: Which function parameter can receive the address of an integer?
s: int *x is a pointer to int.

q: Consider void update(int *p) { *p = 20; }. What does *p = 20 do?
o: Changes the value at the address stored in p
s: It stores 20 in the variable that p points to.

q: Which statement about "call by reference" in C is most accurate?
o: C has built-in reference parameters like C++
C uses pointers to allow a function to modify caller-owned objects
C always passes every argument by address
s: C has no reference parameters. It passes pointers (by value) to achieve the effect.

q: What is the main difference between call by value and pointer-based modification?
o: Call by value passes a copy; a pointer parameter can access the caller's object through its address
Both always modify the caller's variable
Call by value passes source code
s: A copy cannot affect the original. A pointer lets the function reach it.

q: What is the output of this code? int x = 5; void change(int n) { n = 10; } int main(void) { change(x); printf("%d", x); }
s: n is a copy, so x stays 5.

q: What is the output of this code? int x = 5; void change(int *n) { *n = 10; } int main(void) { change(&x); printf("%d", x); }
o: Undefined because pointers cannot be passed
s: change gets the address of x and writes 10 through it.

q: Which is the correct way to call a function that expects an int pointer and should modify variable x?
s: Pass the address: change(&x).

q: What is a function's return value?
o: The value sent back to the calling code
s: It is the value given back by return.

q: Which statement about a void function is correct?
o: It does not return a value to its caller
s: A void function returns nothing but can still take parameters.

q: Which of the following is a standard C library function?
s: strlen is in the standard library. The others are user-defined names.

q: Which header should be included to use strlen()?
s: strlen is declared in string.h.

q: Which statement about recursion and iteration is correct?
o: Both can be used to repeat computations
Iteration always creates a new function call
Recursion never uses a call stack
Recursion cannot have a base case
s: Both repeat work. Recursion uses calls and a stack, iteration uses loops.

q: What is a likely disadvantage of a simple recursive Fibonacci implementation?
s: fib(n-1) and fib(n-2) recompute the same values, giving exponential time.

q: Which practice improves the reliability of recursive functions?
o: Ensuring a correct base case and progress toward it
Using global variables for every value
Calling the function with the same input forever
s: Each call must move closer to a base case that stops the recursion.

q: What does a pointer variable store?
o: The memory address of another variable
s: A pointer holds an address.

q: Which operator gives the address of a variable x?
s: & is the address-of operator.

q: Which declaration creates a pointer to a double?
s: The * in the declaration makes p a pointer to double.

q: If int x = 5; int *p = &x;, what does *p give?
s: *p dereferences the pointer and gives the value of x.

q: What is a NULL pointer?
o: A pointer that points to no object
A pointer that points to address 0 of a valid object
s: NULL is a special value meaning 'points to nothing'. Dereferencing it is undefined behaviour.

q: What is a dangling pointer?
o: A pointer to memory that has been freed or gone out of scope
s: It still holds an address, but the object there no longer exists.

q: What is a wild pointer?
o: A pointer that is always NULL
An uninitialised pointer holding an indeterminate address
s: It was never given a valid address, so using it is dangerous.

q: What does int *p = NULL; followed by *p = 10; cause?
s: Writing through a NULL pointer is undefined behaviour.

q: Which type is a generic pointer that can hold the address of any object type?
s: void * is the generic pointer. It must be cast before dereferencing.

q: Can a void pointer be dereferenced directly?
o: No, it must be cast to a typed pointer first
s: void has no size, so *p on a void pointer is invalid.

q: On a typical 64-bit system, what is sizeof(int *)?
o: Depends on the pointed type, 4 for int
s: All object pointers have the same size, typically 8 bytes on 64-bit systems.

q: If int *p points to a[0] and sizeof(int) is 4, what does p + 1 point to?
s: Pointer arithmetic is scaled by the size of the pointed type, so p + 1 is the next int.
*(p + 2) is the same as a[2], which is 30.

q: In C, a[i] is equivalent to:
s: The subscript operator is defined as *(a + i).

q: What does subtracting two pointers into the same array give?
o: The number of bytes between them
The number of elements between them
s: Pointer difference is measured in elements, not bytes.

q: Which pointer operation is NOT allowed?
o: Subtracting two pointers into the same array
Adding an integer to a pointer
s: Adding two pointers has no meaning and is invalid.

q: What is the output?  int a[] = {1,2,3}; int *p = a; p++; printf("%d", *p);
s: p++ moves p to a[1], which holds 2.

q: What is the output?  int a[] = {4,5,6}; printf("%d", *a + 1);
s: *a is a[0] = 4, and then + 1 gives 5. (Without the parentheses, *a + 1 is not *(a + 1).)

q: What is the difference between *p++ and (*p)++ ?
o: *p++ increments the value; (*p)++ moves the pointer
*p++ moves the pointer after reading; (*p)++ increments the pointed value
s: Postfix ++ binds tighter than *, so *p++ is *(p++). The parentheses make (*p)++ increment the object.

q: How is an array passed to a function in C?
o: A pointer to its first element is passed
Only the first element is copied
s: The array name decays to a pointer to its first element.

q: Inside a function void f(int a[]), sizeof(a) gives:
o: The size of the whole array
s: The parameter is really int *a, so sizeof gives the pointer size.

q: What is a pointer to a pointer?
o: A pointer that holds a value twice
A pointer that holds the address of another pointer
s: int **pp stores the address of an int *.

q: How many * are needed to reach the int value through int **pp?
s: **pp dereferences twice: first to the int *, then to the int.

q: What does const int *p mean?
o: The int pointed to cannot be modified through p
s: It is a pointer to a constant int. The pointer can move, but *p cannot be assigned.

q: What does int *const p mean?
o: The pointer p cannot be changed to point elsewhere
p is a pointer to const
s: It is a constant pointer to int. The value can change, but p is fixed.

q: Which keyword defines a structure?
s: struct groups variables of different types under one name.

q: How do you access a member of a structure variable s?
s: The dot operator is used with a structure variable.

q: How do you access a member through a structure pointer p?
s: -> is used with a pointer. p->name is the same as (*p).name.

q: What is the output?  struct P {int x; int y;} a = {3, 4}; printf("%d", a.x + a.y);
What does typedef struct { int id; } Student; allow?
o: Declaring variables as Student s; without writing struct
s: typedef creates the alias Student, so struct need not be repeated.

q: Why can the size of a structure be larger than the sum of its members?
s: The compiler inserts padding so members are aligned for fast access.

q: On a typical system, what is sizeof(struct {char c; int i;})?
s: char (1) + 3 padding bytes + int (4) = 8.

q: Structures in C can be assigned to each other with = when they have:
s: Assignment copies all members of a structure of the same type.

q: Which statement about passing a structure to a function by value is correct?
s: C passes by value, so the whole structure is copied. Large structures are better passed by pointer.

q: How does a union differ from a structure?
o: It stores members in different files
All members share the same memory
s: A union's members overlap in memory, so only one is meaningful at a time.

q: What is sizeof(union {int i; char c; double d;}) on a typical system?
s: A union is as large as its largest member, which is the 8-byte double.

q: What happens when a union member is assigned after another member was set?
o: The new value overwrites the shared memory
s: Members share storage, so the latest write replaces the old contents.

q: Which header declares malloc() and free()?
s: malloc, calloc, realloc and free are in stdlib.h.

q: What does malloc(n) do?
o: Allocates n bytes without initialising them
Allocates n bytes and sets them to zero
s: malloc reserves uninitialised memory.

q: How does calloc(n, size) differ from malloc?
o: It initialises the memory to zero
s: calloc allocates n x size bytes and sets them to 0.

q: What does realloc(ptr, newsize) do?
o: Changes the size of a previously allocated block
s: It resizes the block, possibly moving it, and returns the new address.

q: What does malloc return when it cannot allocate memory?
s: Always check for NULL before using the result.

q: What is a memory leak?
o: Allocated memory that is never freed
s: The program loses the pointer or forgets free(), so the memory stays reserved.

q: What is a double free?
o: Calling free() twice on the same pointer, which is undefined behaviour
s: Freeing already-freed memory corrupts the heap. Setting the pointer to NULL after free() helps.

q: Dynamic memory is allocated from the:
s: malloc and friends use the heap.

q: Which statement correctly allocates an array of 10 ints dynamically?
s: Multiply the element count by sizeof(int).

q: Which function opens a file in C?
s: fopen(name, mode) returns a FILE pointer.

q: What does fopen return if the file cannot be opened?
s: fopen returns NULL on failure, so always check it.

q: Which mode opens a text file for reading only?
s: "r" reads an existing file. "w" overwrites and "a" appends.

q: What does the mode "w" do if the file already exists?
s: "w" creates the file or erases the existing contents.

q: Which mode appends data at the end of a file?
s: "a" opens for appending, creating the file if needed.

q: Which function closes a file?
s: fclose flushes buffers and releases the file.

q: Which function reads one line of text safely from a file?
s: fgets(buf, size, fp) limits the number of characters read.

q: Which function writes formatted text to a file?
s: fprintf(fp, format, ...) works like printf but writes to fp.

q: What does feof(fp) test?
o: Whether the end of file has been reached
s: It reports the end-of-file indicator of the stream.

q: Which function moves the file position to a given offset?
s: fseek(fp, offset, origin) repositions the stream.

q: What does ftell(fp) return?
o: The current position in the file
s: It returns the current offset from the start of the file.

q: What does rewind(fp) do?
o: Sets the position back to the start of the file
s: rewind is equivalent to fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET) and clears error flags.

q: Which functions are used for binary file input and output?
s: fread and fwrite transfer blocks of bytes.

q: Which mode should be used to open a binary file for reading?
s: The b in "rb" selects binary mode.

q: Which constant is used with fseek to move relative to the end of the file?
s: SEEK_SET is the start, SEEK_CUR the current position, SEEK_END the end.

q: What is the difference between sequential and random access?
o: Random access is only for text
Sequential reads in order; random jumps to any position with fseek
s: Sequential access processes data in order. Random access repositions anywhere.

q: Which symbol begins a preprocessor directive?
s: Directives such as #include and #define start with #.

q: What does #define PI 3.14159 do?
o: Creates a macro that replaces PI with 3.14159 before compilation
s: The preprocessor performs text replacement.

q: What is the output?  #define SQ(x) x*x  printf("%d", SQ(2+3));
s: The macro expands to 2+3*2+3 = 11. Use (x)*(x) to be safe.

q: Why should macro arguments be wrapped in parentheses?
o: To avoid operator-precedence surprises after text replacement
It is required by the compiler
s: Macros are text substitution, so precedence can change the meaning.

q: What is the purpose of an include guard (#ifndef / #define / #endif)?
o: To prevent a header from being included more than once
s: It avoids duplicate-definition errors from repeated inclusion.

q: What is the difference between #include <file.h> and #include "file.h"?
o: Angle brackets search system directories; quotes search the local directory first
Angle brackets are for your own files
s: Quotes look in the current project folder first, then system paths.

q: Which directive undefines a macro?
s: #undef NAME removes a macro definition.

q: What does conditional compilation with #ifdef do?
o: Compiles code only if a macro is defined
s: Code between #ifdef and #endif is included only when the macro exists.

q: Which is a predefined macro that holds the current line number?
s: __LINE__, __FILE__, __DATE__ and __TIME__ are predefined.

q: What is the main difference between a macro and a function?
o: A macro is expanded as text by the preprocessor; a function is called at run time
A function is expanded as text
s: Macros have no type checking and may evaluate arguments more than once.
